title: STAR CAT
oneLiner: Two wizard cats bounce across magic clouds together to catch falling stars before they vanish.
hook: Players must choose whether to bounce toward nearby safe stars or take riskier high arcs for rare gold stars, while coordinating their positions so neither cat-
ramp: Begin with slow, widely spaced stars and stable clouds, then add moving clouds, brief star clusters, and gentle wind lanes one at a time. Alternate 10–15 second pressure bursts with recovery sections;
mechanics: Two players cooperate in one shared vertical arena: each wizard cat automatically bounces whenever it lands on a cloud, while left/right steer the horizontal arc; both can also use A to cast a short horizontal wand burst that collects a star from a little farther away, with a 20-frame cooldown.

Stars fall from the top at bounded speed and disappear after 3.5 seconds. Catching a star scores 100 points for the team and removes it exactly once; a gold star scores 300 and briefly shows a sparkle burst.

Clouds are solid only from above. Cats land on them during a downward arc, bounce upward with a fixed 78-pixel vertical impulse, and wrap at the side edges. Missed clouds cause a fall; a cat is rescued and reset to the lowest cloud if it falls below the playfield, costing one shared rescue.
A cat may spend B once per jump to perform a short air-dash in its facing direction, improving reach but making the landing route harder to control. B resets when the cat lands.

Players have separate three-heart counters. Touching a storm puff or missing the rescue zone costs one heart, flashes the cat for 60 frames, and respawns it on the lowest cloud; the other player continues playing.

The team wins after catching 30 stars or when the 75-second round ends; at timeout, the team keeps its score and receives a clear if at least 24 stars were caught. The team loses when both cats have no hearts, or when the timer ends below 24 stars.

Every 10 seconds the camera scrolls upward to reveal new clouds. The first section has fixed clouds and ordinary stars; later sections add horizontally drifting clouds, then slow storm puffs and gold stars. Never exceed four active stars, three moving clouds, or two storm puffs.

The first star falls directly above a broad starting cloud within 2 seconds, making steering and A collection immediately understandable. Missed stars are replaced by the next bounded spawn, so failure never softlocks the round.
On clear, show total team score and remaining hearts; reset both players, clouds, timer, star IDs, cooldowns, and rescue state for a fresh deterministic round.
artDirection: 256x224 shared vertical arena with a 12-pixel runtime HUD. Each cat is about 20x24 pixels, using a clear wizard-cat silhouette: pointed hat, triangular ears, tail, robe, and a bright wand. Give each player a distinct robe color and hat band. Use the supplied climber/cat asset for the cat identity, drawing wait while airborne or idle and rescued for a successful catch; add a small hat, wand, and colored player marker as aligned sprite details. Clouds are 28–40 pixels wide white-blue platforms with darker undersides. Stars are 8x8 gold four-point pickups with a strong twinkle. Use a deep navy sky, moonlit cloud layers, sparse stars, and a dark quiet region behind active pickups. Show distinct bounce, falling, catch, and hurt poses through simple overlays and squash/stretch primitives; never let effects obscure cloud or star hitboxes.

controls.a: Cast a short wand burst to collect a nearby star; 20-frame cooldown
controls.b: Air-dash once per jump in the facing direction

lose: The team loses when both cats are out of hearts, or the 75-second timer ends with fewer than 24 stars caught.
scoring: Ordinary stars are worth 100 points and gold stars are worth 300; each star scores once when caught.
